title: Table-Based Encodings for Conway's Doomsday Algorithm: Vectorized Doomsdays and Doomyears
summary: Conway's Doomsday Algorithm (1973) determines the day of the week for any date in the Gregorian calendar via three additive components: a century anchor, a year offset, and a month-day offset. The century anchor is a fixed four-entry table. The other two components require live arithmetic: the year offset demands computing $y + \lfloor y/4 \rfloor \pmod{7}$, and the month-day offset requires a subtraction that can produce negative intermediate values.
